nodes.subject: Audio power article
nodes.object: Watts describe electrical power, useful loudness also depends on efficiency, and maximum figures can rise when more distortion is allowed.

support_spans.exact_quote: Audio power is the electrical power transferred from an audio amplifier to a loudspeaker , measured in watts .
The electrical power delivered to the loudspeaker, together with the speaker's efficiency , determines the sound power generated (with the rest of the electrical power being converted to heat).
Considerably more power can be delivered if distortion is allowed to increase; some manufacturers quote maximum power at a higher distortion, like 10%, making their equipment appear more powerful.

nodes.subject: portable-speaker wattage
nodes.object: Electrical watts do not alone establish perceived loudness or clean maximum output; efficiency and allowed distortion matter, and a Max figure is not equivalent to a continuous rating.

accepted_phrases: A portable speaker's watt figure is electrical power, not direct proof of loudness or clean maximum output; efficiency, continuous-versus-maximum measurement, and allowed distortion matter.

nodes.subject: Passive radiator article
nodes.object: A passive radiator is an unwired moving element driven by enclosure pressure and tuned resonance; it can extend bass but has response tradeoffs.

support_spans.exact_quote: A speaker enclosure using a passive radiator usually contains an "active loudspeaker " (or main driver), and a passive radiator (also known as a "drone cone"). The active loudspeaker is a normal driver, and the passive radiator is of similar construction, but without a voice coil and magnet assembly . It is not attached to a voice coil or wired to an electrical circuit or power amplifier .

In the same way as a ported loudspeaker, a passive radiator system uses the sound pressure otherwise trapped in the enclosure to excite a resonance that makes it easier for the speaker system to create the deepest pitches (e.g., basslines ).

nodes.subject: passive radiator
nodes.object: It is a tuned enclosure-pressure mechanism that can help reproduce deep pitches, but the label alone does not establish bass quality or transient performance.

accepted_phrases: A passive radiator is a real tuned enclosure mechanism that can assist low-frequency output, but its presence alone does not prove superior bass quality.

nodes.subject: IP code article
nodes.object: Ingress Protection is a standardized test classification, X means insufficient data for that digit, and water digit 7 covers defined temporary immersion conditions.

support_spans.exact_quote: The IP code or Ingress Protection code indicates how well a device is protected against water and dust.
The digit is replaced with the letter X when insufficient data has been gathered to assign a protection level.

7 Immersion, up to 1 meter (3 ft 3 in) depth Ingress of water in harmful quantity shall not be possible when the enclosure is immersed in water under defined conditions of pressure and time (up to 1 meter (3 ft 3 in) of submersion). Test duration: 30 minutes.

nodes.subject: IPX7 rating
nodes.object: The X supplies no particulate-protection rating, while water digit 7 refers to temporary immersion under defined pressure and time, up to one meter for 30 minutes in the cited table.

accepted_phrases: IPX7 is a bounded temporary-immersion classification, not unlimited waterproofing; X means no particulate-protection level was assigned from the available data.

nodes.subject: Loudspeaker acoustics article
nodes.object: Speaker assessment includes frequency response, off-axis dispersion, sensitivity, maximum power and nonlinear distortion, and room interaction matters.

support_spans.exact_quote: Important driver characteristics are: Frequency response Off-axis response dispersion pattern, lobing Sensitivity (dB SPL for 1 watt input) Maximum power handling Non-linear distortion Colouration (i.e., more or less, delayed resonance ).
It is the performance of a loudspeaker/listening room combination that really matters, as the two interact in multiple ways.

nodes.subject: 360-degree speaker claim
nodes.object: A directional label alone does not establish uniform response or quality because off-axis dispersion, lobing, distortion, sensitivity and room interaction are separate performance dimensions.

accepted_phrases: A 360-degree label is not by itself proof of uniform or superior sound; off-axis dispersion, lobing, distortion, sensitivity, frequency response, and the listening environment still matter.

support_spans.exact_quote: Important driver characteristics are: Frequency response Off-axis response dispersion pattern, lobing Sensitivity (dB SPL for 1 watt input) Maximum power handling Non-linear distortion Colouration (i.e., more or less, delayed resonance ).

nodes.subject: High-resolution audio article
nodes.object: High-resolution audio is defined by source bit depth and sampling frequency, while several wireless codecs marketed as hi-res use lossy compression.

support_spans.exact_quote: High-resolution audio is a term for music files with bit depth greater than 16-bit and sampling frequency higher than 44.1 kHz or 48 kHz used in CD and DVD formats.

Sony's LDAC , Dolby's Digital Plus and Lenbrook's MQA are marketed as "hi-res," [ 9 ] [ 10 ] [ 11 ] however, these codecs employ lossy compression and can often have lower bit rates than Compact Disc Digital Audio , and thus, cannot be classified as "true high-resolution."

nodes.subject: hi-res audio label
nodes.object: The file-format definition concerns source resolution, while a wireless codec can still be lossy; the label alone does not prove the full Bluetooth path.

accepted_phrases: High-resolution audio refers to source bit depth and sample rate; a hi-res label does not by itself establish a lossless end-to-end Bluetooth path.

support_spans.exact_quote: High-resolution audio is a term for music files with bit depth greater than 16-bit and sampling frequency higher than 44.1 kHz or 48 kHz used in CD and DVD formats.

Sony's LDAC , Dolby's Digital Plus and Lenbrook's MQA are marketed as "hi-res," [ 9 ] [ 10 ] [ 11 ] however, these codecs employ lossy compression and can often have lower bit rates than Compact Disc Digital Audio , and thus, cannot be classified as "true high-resolution."

nodes.subject: LDAC article
nodes.object: LDAC is lossy and its best-effort bitrate switches among 330, 660 and 990 kbps depending on connection strength.

support_spans.exact_quote: LDAC is a proprietary , lossy audio coding technology developed by Sony , [ 1 ] designed for streaming audio over Bluetooth connections at up to 990 kbps at 32 bits/96 kHz ( high-resolution audio quality).
By default, LDAC audio bitrate settings are set to Best Effort, which switches between discrete bitrate steps ( CBR ) 330/660/990 kbps depending on connection strength;

nodes.subject: LDAC Bluetooth path
nodes.object: LDAC remains lossy and its default best-effort bitrate changes with connection strength, so a high-resolution source label alone does not establish delivered wireless fidelity.

accepted_phrases: LDAC is a lossy Bluetooth codec whose best-effort bitrate changes with connection strength, so codec support and operating conditions are part of any wireless hi-res claim.

nodes.subject: Postmill speaker-preference thread
nodes.object: One participant preferred a low-cost Tribit speaker, while replies connected preference to bass, subjectivity, listening position, comfort and accuracy.

support_spans.exact_quote: I got an old pair of Bose Quiet Comfort 35 ii, audio technica ath-m50x, and just standard airpod gen 2. All 3 cant compare to my Tribit X Sound Go.

It sounds like you're just a bass head, which is fine, but you have to understand that sound is subjective and you don't have "normal" (no insult intended) audio preferences that would line up with the majority of the public (again no insult) which is fine.

I found speakers with a basic subwoofer to sound better than any of my headphones. It's a different beast entirely, headphones don't have true soundstage, the bass you can feel from your entire body is always better than just hearing and feeling with the ears. The biggest reason I love headphones is the comfort and accuracy. With a speaker even turning my head changes the sound to a point where I'd rather use a headphone.

nodes.subject: Postmill Bluetooth-codec thread
nodes.object: Participants ask for controlled testing rather than bitrate assumptions and note that real-world congestion can change codec performance.

support_spans.exact_quote: How were your assessments of which codec sounds better made, exactly? Did you conduct any controlled testing, or were you just basing them on the assumption that high bitrate = sounds better?

As for Bluetooth, I think that there's a HUGE difference between what can sound best, and what will sound best in most average situations, like in an airport or a gym, where network congestion plays a huge role, which is why I tried to also include how it sounds to the ear, in real life scenarios, not just in theory.

nodes.subject: Soundcore Flare 2 claim audit
nodes.object: The route costs $53.49 and publishes 20W as 10W by two plus THD+N below one percent, making its output claim narrower than a Max-only headline; the listing still omits the THD test condition and remains seller evidence.

nodes.subject: Ortizan 40W claim audit
nodes.object: The route costs $57.99, but its 40W headline is specified as two 20W Max channels and its distortion-free-at-maximum claim lacks a disclosed THD threshold or continuous-power test condition.

nodes.subject: speaker marketing claim boundaries
nodes.object: Passive radiators and dispersion are real design concepts but their labels alone do not establish bass quality or uniform 360-degree response; a hi-res source label also does not establish a lossless, supported or stable Bluetooth path.

nodes.subject: poolside and community evidence scope
nodes.object: Both listings claim IPX7, whose cited definition is bounded temporary immersion; the two captured community threads concern general preference and codec methodology and cannot be represented as same-model pool or beach validation.
